transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. Thanks for making time. As you know, Press 5 has been throwing intermittent servo-drive alarms over the last two production weeks, and we do have a replacement servo retrofit kit sitting in the maintenance storeroom ready to go. We've got the Saturday maintenance window from 06:00 to 16:00 available, and the decision on whether to take Press 5 offline for the retrofit is mine to make. Before I finalize the work order, I want to hear from each of you. Controls engineering — what's your read on the alarms and the retrofit? Production planning — what's the impact if Press 5 is down Saturday, and what's the status of Press 2? Safety — any concerns with this retrofit? Quality — any issues on parts coming off Press 5 lately? Let's go around the table.
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: Elena, I completed the controls bench test this morning. The retrofit will require exactly 2 hours for controller-parameter backup and restoration, followed by exactly 6 hours of controlled commissioning — so 8 hours total. That fits within the 06:00 to 16:00 window, but with no margin to spare. I should also note I haven't attached the bench-test note to the work order yet, but I can do that as soon as we're done here.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I need to share some critical scheduling information. This morning I confirmed the released schedule: 480 housings are due for Monday shipment. Press 2 can make exactly 240 of them on Saturday, and the remaining 240 must be assigned to Press 5 after the retrofit. I haven't updated the shared schedule yet because the maintenance decision was still open. So if Press 5 is taken down for the full 8-hour retrofit on Saturday, we'd still need it back online to produce those 240 housings — meaning the retrofit would need to be completed within the window and Press 5 available for production afterward, or we'd have a shortfall for Monday's shipment.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: Elena, before we finalize anything, I need to flag a safety item. I completed a Saturday arc-flash review for Press 5's electrical cabinet yesterday, but I haven't entered it in the safety permit yet. That review requires a documented lockout with zero-energy verification by two authorized employees, plus a 1.5-meter exclusion boundary around Press 5's electrical cabinet. This is critical for the retrofit — the servo drive work will involve accessing that cabinet, so these lockout and exclusion requirements need to be built into the work order and scheduled within the 8-hour window Ravi just described.
